steps.title: Polite or friendly you
steps.how_to: How to greet and ask after someone politely or in a friendly way.
steps.intro: You'll learn two ways to say 'How are you?', one polite and one friendly. You'll use the polite one with most adults you meet at the shop or market.

examples.en: Good morning, ma'am. How are you?
How's it going? How are you?

steps.notice: With shopkeepers, older people and strangers, you say «¿Cómo está?» and «¿Y usted?». With friends, children and people your age who use tú with you first, it's «¿Cómo estás?» and «¿Y tú?». Wait until the other person says tú to you.
steps.context: In Mexico, using usted is a sign of respect, not distance.

ask.said: ¿Cómo saludas a una señora mayor?
ask.en: How do you greet an older lady?

answer.en: Good morning, ma'am. How are you?

ask.said: ¿Cómo le preguntas a un amigo cómo está?
ask.en: How do you ask a friend how he is?

ask.said: ¿Cómo te despides de una señora mayor?
ask.en: How do you say goodbye to an older lady?

answer.said: Hasta luego. Que le vaya bien.

mission.goal: Greet the shopkeeper politely and ask how they are.

say.en: Good morning, ma'am. How are you?

steps.title: Saying how you are
steps.how_to: How to say how you are feeling.
steps.intro: You'll be able to answer when someone asks how you are. People ask this in shops, cafés and on the stairs.
steps.notice: To say how you are, you use «estoy», and the question uses «está» or «estás». «Estoy bien, gracias» is the phrase to remember.

ask.said: ¿Cómo estás?
ask.en: How are you?

ask.said: ¿Cómo estás hoy?
ask.en: How are you today?

ask.said: Soy una señora. ¿Cómo me preguntas cómo estoy?
ask.en: I'm a lady. How do you ask me how I am?

mission.goal: Answer when someone asks how you are.

steps.title: Hello at any hour
steps.how_to: How to greet people in the morning, afternoon or evening.
steps.intro: You'll be able to say hello at the right time of day, or with one short word that works at any time. You'll use it every time you walk into a shop.
steps.notice: Buenos días goes until about noon. Buenas tardes starts at noon and lasts until dark. Buenas noches is the hello once it's dark, and also a goodbye. «Buenas» works at any hour.
steps.context: A quick «buenas» is enough when you walk into a small shop.

ask.said: ¿Cómo saludas a las diez de la mañana?
ask.en: How do you greet people at ten in the morning?

ask.said: ¿Cómo saludas a la una de la tarde?
ask.en: How do you greet people at one in the afternoon?

ask.said: ¿Cómo saludas a las ocho de la noche?
ask.en: How do you greet people at eight at night?

mission.goal: Greet the shopkeeper as you walk in.

steps.title: Greeting a whole group
steps.how_to: How to greet and ask after two or more people.
steps.intro: You'll be able to talk to a group, like a family or a shop full of people. In Mexico any group gets the same form.
steps.notice: For two or more people, you say «están» and «les». Mexicans do this even with friends and children.

ask.said: Entras a una tienda llena de gente a las cuatro. ¿Cómo saludas?
ask.en: You walk into a shop full of people at four. How do you greet them?

ask.said: ¿Cómo les preguntas a dos amigos cómo están?
ask.en: How do you ask two friends how they are?

ask.said: ¿Cómo te despides de un grupo?
ask.en: How do you say goodbye to a group?

mission.goal: Greet everyone in a shop with several people.

steps.title: A Mexican goodbye
steps.how_to: How to say goodbye with «Que le vaya bien».
steps.intro: You'll be able to leave a shop or say goodbye to a neighbour the way people do here. You'll also know how to answer when someone says it to you.

examples.said: Hasta luego. Que le vaya bien.

steps.notice: Learn «Que le vaya bien» as one whole phrase and only change «le» to «te» for a friend or «les» for a group. When someone says it to you, answer «Gracias, igualmente».
steps.context: People say goodbye when they leave a small shop.

ask.said: ¿Cómo te despides de una señora en una tienda?
ask.en: How do you say goodbye to a lady in a shop?

answer.said: Hasta luego. Que le vaya bien.

ask.said: Un amigo te dice «Que te vaya bien». ¿Qué respondes?
ask.en: A friend says «Que te vaya bien» to you. What do you answer?

ask.said: ¿Cómo te despides de un amigo?
ask.en: How do you say goodbye to a friend?

mission.goal: Say goodbye to the shopkeeper as you leave.

say.said: Hasta luego. Que le vaya bien.

steps.title: Say you didn't understand
steps.how_to: How to tell someone you didn't understand and ask them to slow down.
steps.intro: You'll learn three short phrases to use the moment someone speaks too fast. You can say them at a taco stand, a shop or anywhere else.

examples.en: What do you want in your tacos?

steps.notice: Each phrase works exactly as it is, from your very first day. Say it in Spanish just as you heard it here.
steps.context: Newcomers are expected to ask, and most people slow down and rephrase gladly.

ask.said: ¿Qué dices si no entiendes?
ask.en: What do you say if you don't understand?

ask.said: ¿Qué dices si alguien habla muy rápido?
ask.en: What do you say if someone speaks very fast?

ask.said: ¿Cómo pides que lo digan otra vez?
ask.en: How do you ask them to say it again?

mission.goal: Tell the taquero you didn't understand and ask for slower.

say.said: Perdón, no entendí. Más despacio, por favor.
say.en: Sorry, I didn't understand. More slowly, please.

steps.title: Saying pardon the Mexican way
steps.how_to: How to use ¿Mande? to ask for a repeat and to answer when someone calls you.
steps.intro: You'll learn one polite word that does two jobs. You can say it when you missed something, or when someone calls to you.
steps.notice: ¿Mande? asks for a repeat and also answers a call. With older people, ¿mande? or ¿perdón? sounds polite.
steps.context: Asking ¿mande? is normal for a newcomer and people take it well.

ask.said: ¿Cómo pides que repitan algo, con una palabra?
ask.en: How do you ask for a repeat with one word?

ask.said: Si un vendedor te llama, ¿qué contestas?
ask.en: If a vendor calls you, what do you answer?

ask.said: ¿Qué le dices a una señora si no la entendiste?
ask.en: What do you say to a woman if you didn't understand her?

mission.goal: Ask a vendor to repeat what they said.

steps.title: Asking someone to repeat it
steps.how_to: How to ask someone to repeat or write something using me lo.
steps.intro: You'll learn a polite request that works for repeating, writing and saying again. You can use it whenever you miss a word.

examples.en: Could you say that again, please?
Could you write it for me?
Can you say it again? (to a neighbour)

steps.notice: Me lo always stays together, right before the verb. With a neighbour or a friend, use puedes instead of puede.
steps.context: ¿Me lo repite? is a normal request, and people take it well.

ask.said: ¿Qué dices para pedir que repitan algo?
ask.en: What do you say to ask someone to repeat something?

answer.en: Could you say that again, please?

ask.said: ¿Cómo pides que lo escriban?
ask.en: How do you ask them to write it down?

answer.en: Could you write it for me?

ask.said: ¿Cómo le pides a un vecino que lo repita?
ask.en: How do you ask a neighbour to repeat it?

mission.goal: Ask the shopkeeper to say it again.

say.en: Could you say that again, please?

steps.title: Polite requests with puede
steps.how_to: How to ask someone politely to do something with ¿Me puede…?
steps.intro: You'll learn a simple pattern for polite requests. You can use it to ask for help or for a slower pace.

examples.en: Can you help me? (to a neighbour)

steps.notice: Use puede for someone you address as usted and puedes for a neighbour. The next verb always ends in -r, as in repetir, hablar and ayudar. So you say ¿Puede repetir, por favor?

ask.said: ¿Cómo le pides ayuda a un vecino?
ask.en: How do you ask a neighbour for help?

ask.said: Si alguien habla rápido, ¿qué le preguntas, con usted?
ask.en: If someone speaks fast, what do you ask them, politely?

ask.said: ¿Cómo le pides a la señora de la tienda que repita?
ask.en: How do you ask the shop lady to repeat?

mission.goal: Ask the ticket clerk to speak more slowly.

steps.title: Spelling words out loud
steps.how_to: How to spell words aloud with Spanish letter names.
steps.intro: You'll learn how to spell your name and ask how a word is spelled. You'll use it for forms, orders and new words.

examples.en: Could you spell your surname, please?

examples.said: Doble u, e, be grande, be grande.

examples.en: How do you spell it? With a B?

examples.said: Sí: be grande, a, ene, cu, u, e, te, a.
examples.en: Yes: B, A, N, Q, U, E, T, A.

steps.notice: Spanish letters have their own names, and the vowels sound like eh and ee. Say doble u for W, be grande for B and ve chica for V. 'Webb' is doble u, e, be grande, be grande.
steps.context: B and V sound the same, so Mexicans say be grande and ve chica to tell them apart.

ask.said: Cuando deletreas, ¿cómo dices la V?
ask.en: When you spell, how do you say V?

ask.said: ¿Cómo deletreas «Webb»?
ask.en: How do you spell 'Webb'?

answer.said: Doble u, e, be grande, be grande.

ask.said: Para saber si lleva B o V, ¿qué preguntas?
ask.en: To find out if it has a B or a V, what do you ask?

answer.said: ¿Cómo se escribe? ¿Con be grande o con ve chica?
answer.en: How do you spell it? With a B or a V?

mission.goal: Ask a neighbour how a word is spelled.

say.said: ¿Cómo se escribe? ¿Con be grande o con ve chica?
say.en: How do you spell it? With a B or a V?

steps.title: Say and ask names
steps.how_to: How to say your name and ask someone else's.
steps.intro: Now you'll be able to give your name and ask for theirs when you meet a neighbour or someone new. You'll use it the moment you're introduced.

examples.en: My name's Rosa. Nice to meet you.
Hi, I'm Diego. What's your name? (tú)

steps.notice: Names go with me llamo, with the me always there. Ask with ¿cómo se llama? for usted and ¿cómo te llamas? for tú. Answer mucho gusto with igualmente.

ask.said: ¿Cómo te llamas?
ask.en: What's your name?

ask.said: ¿Cómo le preguntas el nombre a una señora mayor?
ask.en: How do you ask an older lady her name?

ask.said: Te dicen «mucho gusto». ¿Qué contestas?
ask.en: They say 'nice to meet you'. What do you answer?

mission.goal: Tell a neighbour your name and ask theirs.

steps.title: Say where you're from
steps.how_to: How to say which place you come from.
steps.intro: You'll be able to say where you're from and ask others the same. People will ask you this early on, so it's worth having ready.

examples.said: Soy de Chicago, pero ahora vivo aquí.
examples.en: I'm from Chicago, but I live here now.

steps.notice: Soy de plus a place tells where you come from, and the question starts with de dónde. Use a city or a country: Soy de Canadá.

ask.said: ¿De dónde eres?
ask.en: Where are you from?

ask.said: ¿Cómo le preguntas a una señora de dónde es?
ask.en: How do you ask a lady where she's from?

ask.said: ¿Eres de aquí?
ask.en: Are you from here?

answer.said: No, soy de …, pero ahora vivo aquí.
answer.en: No, I'm from …, but I live here now.

mission.goal: Tell a neighbour where you're from and that you live here now.

say.said: Soy de …, pero ahora vivo aquí.
say.en: I'm from …, but I live here now.

steps.title: Say where you live
steps.how_to: How to say and ask where someone lives.
steps.intro: You'll be able to say which neighbourhood you live in and ask others where they live. It comes up with neighbours and at any counter where they take your details.

examples.en: I live in the Centro neighbourhood.
I live here, near the market.

steps.notice: Vivo is for I, vives for tú and vive for usted. Add en and the place: vivo en esta colonia.
steps.context: Every address includes the colonia, which matters more than the street name for finding a place.

ask.said: ¿Dónde vives?
ask.en: Where do you live?

ask.said: ¿Cómo le preguntas a una vecina mayor dónde vive?
ask.en: How do you ask an older neighbour where she lives?

ask.said: ¿Vives aquí?
ask.en: Do you live here?

answer.said: Sí, vivo aquí, en la colonia …
answer.en: Yes, I live here, in the … neighbourhood.

mission.goal: Tell someone which neighbourhood you live in.

steps.title: Say how long you've been here
steps.how_to: How to say how much time you've spent in Mexico.
steps.intro: You'll be able to say how long you've been here and understand when someone asks. Neighbours and new friends ask this early on.

examples.en: How long have you been here? (usted)
How long have you been in Mexico? (tú)
I've been in Mexico a month.

steps.notice: Say llevo or tengo plus the time, then aquí or en México. Llevo dos semanas aquí works just as well as tengo dos semanas aquí.
steps.context: People here often ask early on how long you've been here.

ask.said: ¿Llevas mucho tiempo aquí?
ask.en: Have you been here a long time?

ask.said: ¿Cuánto tiempo llevas en México?
ask.en: How long have you been in Mexico?

ask.said: ¿Cómo le preguntas a una vecina desde cuándo está aquí?
ask.en: How do you ask a neighbour since when she's been here?

answer.en: How long have you been here? (usted)

mission.goal: Tell a neighbour how long you've been here.

steps.title: Ask the key questions
steps.how_to: How to ask someone's name, origin, home and time here.
steps.intro: You'll be able to ask the main getting-to-know-you questions yourself, with tú, to someone your age. Use them to keep a chat going after you've answered.

examples.en: How long have you been here?

steps.notice: The question word comes first and has a written accent: cómo, dónde, cuánto. For origin the de goes in front: ¿de dónde eres? Ask a name with cómo: ¿cómo te llamas?

ask.said: Quieres saber el nombre de un chico en una fiesta. ¿Qué le preguntas?
ask.en: You want to know a guy's name at a party. What do you ask him?

ask.said: Quieres saber la ciudad de origen de un amigo. ¿Qué le preguntas?
ask.en: You want to know where a friend comes from. What do you ask?

ask.said: Quieres saber desde cuándo está aquí un amigo. ¿Qué le preguntas?
ask.en: You want to know since when a friend has been here. What do you ask?

answer.en: How long have you been here?

mission.goal: Ask someone their name and where they're from.

say.en: What's your name? Where are you from?

steps.title: Excuse me, sorry, thanks
steps.how_to: How to use the right polite phrase for getting past, getting attention and saying sorry.
steps.intro: English uses one phrase, excuse me, where Spanish uses three. You'll be able to move through a crowded bus, call someone over, or say sorry after a bump.

examples.en: Excuse me, could you help me with something?

steps.notice: Con permiso is for getting past or leaving. Disculpe gets someone's attention. Perdón is for after a bump or a mistake.
steps.context: Mexican courtesy is constant and small, and people say con permiso whenever they pass someone or leave a table.

ask.said: ¿Qué dices para pasar entre la gente?
ask.en: What do you say to get past people?

ask.said: Chocas con alguien sin querer. ¿Qué dices?
ask.en: You bump into someone by accident. What do you say?

ask.said: Necesitas ayuda en una tienda. ¿Qué dices?
ask.en: You need help in a shop. What do you say?

answer.en: Excuse me, could you help me with something?

mission.goal: Ask to get past people.

steps.title: Disculpe or disculpa
steps.how_to: How to get someone's attention politely with disculpe, disculpa or disculpen.
steps.intro: You'll be able to call someone over politely, whether it's a stranger, a friend or a whole group. You'll use it in shops, in the plaza and at market stalls.

examples.en: Excuse me, could you help me with something?
Excuse me, can you help me?

steps.notice: With a shopkeeper or a stranger, say disculpe and ¿me ayuda? With friends and people your age who use tú, say disculpa and ¿me ayudas? To a group, say disculpen.

ask.said: ¿Qué dices para llamar a un señor en la calle?
ask.en: What do you say to call over a man in the street?

ask.said: ¿Cómo pides ayuda a un amigo?
ask.en: How do you ask a friend for help?

answer.en: Excuse me, can you help me?

ask.said: ¿Qué dices para llamar la atención de un grupo?
ask.en: What do you say to get a group's attention?

mission.goal: Get a vendor's attention and ask for help.

say.en: Excuse me, could you help me with something?

steps.title: Softening with a little -ito
steps.how_to: How to make a request sound softer with momentito, poquito and ahorita.
steps.intro: You'll be able to ask for a moment or say a little bit in a friendly, polite way. You'll use it at the pharmacy, at the taquería and when someone is waiting for you.

examples.en: Right now. / In a little while.

steps.notice: Adding -ito makes a request or an amount sound smaller and politer. It isn't literal: un momentito can be several minutes, and ahorita can mean now, soon or later.

ask.said: Necesitas tiempo para buscar tu dinero. ¿Qué dices?
ask.en: You need time to find your money. What do you say?

ask.said: ¿Hablas español?
ask.en: Do you speak Spanish?

ask.said: ¿Cuándo pagas?
ask.en: When are you paying?

mission.goal: Ask the pharmacist to wait a moment.

steps.title: Calling people by title
steps.how_to: How to address people with joven, señora, don and doña.
steps.intro: You'll be able to speak to people the way Mexicans do, with a title instead of a name. You'll use it with strangers, shopkeepers and older neighbours.

examples.en: Excuse me, young man, could you help me?

steps.notice: Use joven, señor or señora for people you don't know. Use don or doña with the first name for older people you know, like doña Lupita.
steps.context: Market staff often call you joven, señorita, güero or güera as they call you over, and it's friendly sales talk.

ask.said: Necesitas ayuda de un chico en la calle. ¿Qué dices?
ask.en: You need help from a young guy in the street. What do you say?

answer.en: Excuse me, young man, could you help me?

ask.said: ¿Cómo llamas a una mujer mayor que no conoces?
ask.en: How do you address an older woman you don't know?

ask.said: Tu vecina mayor se llama Lupita. ¿Cómo le das las gracias?
ask.en: Your older neighbour is called Lupita. How do you thank her?

mission.goal: Greet the shopkeeper with a polite title.

steps.title: What shop staff ask you
steps.how_to: How to understand and answer ¿Qué buscaba? in a shop.
steps.intro: You'll be able to answer when shop staff call you in and ask what you need. You'll hear it at shops and market stalls.

examples.en: Come in! What were you looking for?

steps.notice: Shop staff ask in the past to sound softer. You just answer in the present: say what you want, or say you're just looking.
steps.context: Shop and market staff call out ¡pásele! to bring you in.

ask.said: ¿Qué buscas en la tienda?
ask.en: What are you looking for in the shop?

ask.said: Entras a una tienda y solo quieres mirar. ¿Qué dices?
ask.en: You go into a shop and only want to look. What do you say?

ask.said: ¿Qué necesitas hoy?
ask.en: What do you need today?

mission.goal: Tell the shopkeeper you're just looking.

steps.title: Order food politely
steps.how_to: How to ask for food and drinks politely with me da.
steps.intro: In this step you'll learn the phrase you'll use at every counter, taco stand and café. It lets you ask for what you want in a polite way.

examples.en: Hi! What can I get you?

examples.said: Me da tres tacos de pastor, por favor.
examples.en: Can I have three al pastor tacos, please?

examples.said: Me da un café, por favor.
examples.en: Can I have a coffee, please?

examples.said: Me da una torta para llevar.
examples.en: Can I have a torta to go?

steps.notice: Every order starts with me da, then what you want, and por favor goes with it. Me da with por favor is the polite way to order from a stranger.
steps.context: Orders usually start with a greeting such as Buenas tardes.

ask.said: ¿Qué quieres comer en la taquería?
ask.en: What do you want to eat at the taquería?

answer.said: Me da tres tacos de pastor, por favor.
answer.en: Can I have three al pastor tacos, please?

ask.said: ¿Qué pides en un café por la mañana?
ask.en: What do you order at a café in the morning?

answer.said: Me da un café, por favor.
answer.en: Can I have a coffee, please?

ask.said: ¿Cómo pides una torta si no te quedas a comer?
ask.en: How do you ask for a torta if you're not staying to eat?

answer.said: Me da una torta para llevar, por favor.
answer.en: Can I have a torta to go, please?

mission.goal: Order three tacos at the stand.

say.said: Buenas tardes. Me da tres tacos de pastor, por favor.
say.en: Good afternoon. Can I have three al pastor tacos, please?

steps.title: Counting what you order
steps.how_to: How to say one, a or several of what you order.
steps.intro: Here you'll learn to order one thing or more than one. You'll say it every time you ask for tacos, a torta or a drink.

examples.said: Me da dos tacos de bistec, por favor.
examples.en: Can I have two steak tacos, please?

examples.said: Me da una torta de milanesa.
examples.en: Can I have a milanesa torta?

examples.said: Un agua de horchata y un café de olla, por favor.
examples.en: An horchata and a café de olla, please.

examples.said: Me da dos limones, por favor.
examples.en: Can I have two limes, please?

steps.notice: Use un for one and una for a feminine word like torta. To make more than one, add -s after a vowel, as in tacos, and -es after a consonant, as in limones. For agua the phrase is un agua de horchata.
steps.context: Limón in Mexico is the small green lime.

ask.said: ¿Cuántos tacos quieres?
ask.en: How many tacos do you want?

answer.said: Me da dos tacos, por favor.
answer.en: Can I have two tacos, please?

ask.said: ¿Cuántas tortas quieres?
ask.en: How many tortas do you want?

answer.said: Me da una torta, por favor.
answer.en: Can I have one torta, please?

ask.said: ¿Qué bebida pides?
ask.en: What drink do you order?

answer.said: Un agua de horchata, por favor.

mission.goal: Order a torta and a water.

say.said: Me da una torta y un agua de jamaica, por favor.
say.en: Can I have a torta and a jamaica water, please?

steps.title: Name the filling
steps.how_to: How to say what a taco, torta or drink is filled with or made of.
steps.intro: You'll learn how to name the filling or flavour of what you order. You'll use it at the taco stand, the torta stand and the agua fresca counter.

examples.said: Me da tres tacos de pastor, por favor.
examples.en: Can I have three al pastor tacos, please?

examples.said: Me da dos tacos de bistec.
examples.en: Can I have two steak tacos?

examples.said: Un agua de jamaica, por favor.

steps.notice: The food comes first, then de, then the filling or flavour: tacos de pastor, torta de jamón, agua de jamaica. Spanish puts the filling after the food, the other way round from English.
steps.context: People also say tacos al pastor.

ask.said: ¿Qué tacos quieres?
ask.en: Which tacos do you want?

ask.said: ¿Qué torta pides?
ask.en: Which torta do you order?

answer.said: Una torta de jamón, por favor.

ask.said: ¿Qué agua fresca pides?
ask.en: Which agua fresca do you order?

answer.said: Un agua de jamaica, por favor.

mission.goal: Order tacos with a filling you choose.

say.said: Me da dos tacos de bistec, por favor.
say.en: Can I have two steak tacos, please?

steps.title: With or without
steps.how_to: How to say with or without something when you order.
steps.intro: This step gives you two small words that let you say how you want your food or drink. You'll use them when the taquero or the barista asks what goes in it.
steps.notice: Con means with and sin means without. Both go straight before the food: con todo, sin cebolla, sin azúcar.
steps.context: Con todo means with onion and cilantro.

ask.said: ¿Cómo quieres los tacos?
ask.en: How do you want your tacos?

ask.said: ¿Qué no quieres en tus tacos?
ask.en: What don't you want in your tacos?

ask.said: ¿Cómo tomas el café?
ask.en: How do you take your coffee?

answer.said: Un café sin azúcar, por favor.

mission.goal: Order tacos and say what you don't want on them.

steps.title: Ask for small extras
steps.how_to: How to ask for small things like a napkin with me regala.
steps.intro: You'll learn a soft way to ask for little extras at a stand or counter. It helps when you need a napkin, a bag or a water.

examples.en: Could I have a still water?
Could I have a little bag?

steps.notice: Say ¿Me regala…? and then the small thing you need. It does not mean the thing is free, and you still pay for what has a price. If you're ever unsure, ¿Me da…? works everywhere.
steps.context: In central Mexico, ¿me regala…? is a soft way to ask for small things.

ask.said: ¿Qué pides si necesitas limpiarte las manos?
ask.en: What do you ask for if you need to wipe your hands?

ask.said: ¿Cómo pides una bolsa pequeña?
ask.en: How do you ask for a small bag?

answer.en: Could I have a little bag?

ask.said: ¿Qué pides si quieres un agua sin sabor?
ask.en: What do you ask for if you want a water with no flavour?

answer.en: Could I have a still water?

mission.goal: Ask the taquero for a napkin.
